question: Compare NVIDIA's and AMD's revenue in 2025.
answer:
NVIDIA's revenue for the year ended January 25, 2026 was about $215.9 billion. AMD's revenue for the year ended December 27, 2025 was about $34.6 billion. I matched these by end date because NVIDIA's "FY2026" is the year closest to calendar 2025. NVIDIA's revenue was roughly 6.2 times AMD's (215,938 ÷ 34,639 ≈ 6.23).

## What the filing says
- NVIDIA reported revenue of $215,938 million for fiscal 2026, the year ended 2026-01-25 [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].
- AMD reported net revenue of $34,639 million for fiscal 2025, the year ended 2025-12-27 [Advanced Micro Devices FY2025 10-K, p.74].
- The gap is about $181,299 million (215,938 − 34,639).
- NVIDIA's revenue grew 65.5%, from $130,497 million to $215,938 million [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].
- AMD's revenue grew 34.3%, from $25,785 million to $34,639 million [Advanced Micro Devices FY2025 10-K, p.74].

Revenue here is the total sales a company reports on its income statement before any costs are subtracted.

## What this might mean
In the periods compared, NVIDIA was much larger than AMD and also grew faster. The two years don't line up exactly, since NVIDIA's ended about a month after AMD's. I'd treat the comparison as approximate. Revenue alone says nothing about profitability or what drove the sales.

question: Which company invests more in research and development, NVIDIA or AMD?
answer:
NVIDIA spends more on R&D in dollars: $18,497 million in its fiscal year ended 25 January 2026, against AMD's $8,091 million in its fiscal year ended 27 December 2025. The two years end about a month apart, so they roughly overlap. AMD spends more relative to its size.

## What the filing says
- NVIDIA's R&D (the cost of designing new products and technology) was $18,497 million in FY2026 [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].
- AMD's R&D was $8,091 million in FY2025 [Advanced Micro Devices FY2025 10-K, p.74].
- NVIDIA's figure is about 2.3 times AMD's (18,497 ÷ 8,091 ≈ 2.29).
- As a share of revenue, AMD's R&D was 23.4% ($8,091M ÷ $34,639M) [Advanced Micro Devices FY2025 10-K, p.74].
- NVIDIA's R&D was 8.6% of revenue ($18,497M ÷ $215,938M) [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].

## What this might mean
In absolute dollars, NVIDIA puts far more money into R&D. NVIDIA's revenue is much larger, though (about 6.2 times AMD's: 215,938 ÷ 34,639). That is why AMD's R&D takes a bigger slice of its revenue even though it spends less. Which measure matters depends on whether you care about total spending power or how much of the business goes into R&D.

question: Is Tesla more profitable than Apple?
answer:
Apple was far more profitable than Tesla in its latest fiscal year. Apple earned about $112.0 billion in net income, against Tesla's $3.8 billion. The two years end on different dates: Apple's ended Sept 27, 2025 and Tesla's ended Dec 31, 2025.

## What the filing says
- **Net income (profit after all costs and taxes):** Apple reported $112,010 million [Apple FY2025 10-K, p.32]. Tesla reported $3,794 million attributable to common stockholders [Tesla FY2025 10-K, p.53].
- **Net margin (net income ÷ revenue):** Apple's was 26.9% ($112,010M ÷ $416,161M) [Apple FY2025 10-K, p.32]. Tesla's was 4.0% ($3,794M ÷ $94,827M) [Tesla FY2025 10-K, p.53].
- **Operating margin (profit from core operations before interest and taxes, as a share of revenue):** Apple's was 32.0% ($133,050M ÷ $416,161M) [Apple FY2025 10-K, p.32]. Tesla's was 4.6% ($4,355M ÷ $94,827M) [Tesla FY2025 10-K, p.53].
- **Gross margin (revenue left after the direct cost of making the products):** Apple's was 46.9% ($195,201M ÷ $416,161M) [Apple FY2025 10-K, p.32]. Tesla's was 18.0% ($17,094M ÷ $94,827M) [Tesla FY2025 10-K, p.53].

## What this might mean
Apple led on every measure I checked, in dollars and as a share of revenue. Tesla's revenue was roughly a quarter of Apple's ($94.8B vs. $416.2B), but its profit was far smaller still. Apple kept about 27 cents of each revenue dollar as net profit, while Tesla kept about 4 cents.

question: How did Google do compared with Microsoft this year?
answer:
Comparing each company's latest fiscal year, Alphabet (Google's parent) had higher revenue than Microsoft. Microsoft had higher profit, a higher operating margin and slightly faster revenue growth. The periods don't line up exactly. Alphabet's year ended 31 Dec 2025 and Microsoft's ended 30 Jun 2026, so Microsoft's year ends six months later.

## What the filing says
- **Revenue:** Alphabet had $402,836M and Microsoft had $331,839M. [Alphabet FY2025 10-K, p.84; Microsoft FY2026 10-K, p.50]
- **Revenue growth:** Microsoft grew 17.8% ($281,724M to $331,839M). Alphabet grew 15.1% ($350,018M to $402,836M). [Microsoft FY2026 10-K, p.50; Alphabet FY2025 10-K, p.84]
- **Operating margin** (operating income as a share of revenue): Microsoft was 46.8% ($155,237M ÷ $331,839M). Alphabet was 32.0% ($129,039M ÷ $402,836M). [Microsoft FY2026 10-K, p.50; Alphabet FY2025 10-K, p.84]
- **Net income** (profit after all costs and taxes): Microsoft had $133,749M and Alphabet had $132,170M. [Microsoft FY2026 10-K, p.50; Alphabet FY2025 10-K, p.84]
- **Net income growth:** Alphabet grew 32.0% ($100,118M to $132,170M). Microsoft grew 31.3% ($101,832M to $133,749M). [Alphabet FY2025 10-K, p.84; Microsoft FY2026 10-K, p.50]

## What this might mean
Alphabet is the bigger business by sales, but Microsoft kept more of each revenue dollar as operating profit. That is why Microsoft's net income was slightly higher on less revenue. Profit growth was almost the same for both, so neither clearly pulled ahead on that measure. These figures don't explain the reasons behind the numbers, and the year-end gap makes the comparison approximate.

question: Rank the companies by operating margin.
answer:
Using each company's latest fiscal year, NVIDIA ranks first on operating margin at 60.4% and Walmart ranks last at 4.3%. Operating margin is operating income divided by revenue. It shows how much of each sales dollar is left after running costs, before interest and taxes.

## What the filing says
Fiscal years end on different dates, so I matched each company by its own latest year-end.

1. NVIDIA (year ended 2026-01-25): 60.4%, or 130,387 ÷ 215,938 [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].
2. Microsoft (2026-06-30): 46.8%, or 155,237 ÷ 331,839 [Microsoft FY2026 10-K, p.50].
3. Alphabet (2025-12-31): 32.0%, or 129,039 ÷ 402,836 [Alphabet FY2025 10-K, p.84].
4. Apple (2025-09-27): 32.0%, or 133,050 ÷ 416,161 [Apple FY2025 10-K, p.32].
5. Expedia Group (2025-12-31): 12.7%, or 1,871 ÷ 14,733 [Expedia Group FY2025 10-K, p.79].
6. Amazon.com (2025-12-31): 11.2%, or 79,975 ÷ 716,924 [Amazon.com FY2025 10-K, p.37].
7. Advanced Micro Devices (2025-12-27): 10.7%, or 3,694 ÷ 34,639 [Advanced Micro Devices FY2025 10-K, p.74].
8. Tesla (2025-12-31): 4.6%, or 4,355 ÷ 94,827 [Tesla FY2025 10-K, p.53].
9. Walmart (2025-01-31): 4.3%, or 29,348 ÷ 680,985 [Walmart FY2025 10-K, p.83].

- Alphabet and Apple both round to 32.0%. My unrounded figures are 32.03% for Alphabet and 31.97% for Apple, which is why Alphabet is placed ahead.
- JPMorgan Chase isn't ranked. It is a bank, and its statements have no comparable operating income line.
- Walmart's latest year ended January 2025, earlier than the others.

## What this might mean
This is my own reading. The spread is wide. NVIDIA and Microsoft keep far more of each sales dollar as operating profit than the companies at the bottom. A low margin doesn't mean a small business: Walmart and Amazon have the largest revenues here but thin margins. Margins also don't show absolute profit.
